answer: Persistent compute attestation. Each identity must continuously run a verified workload whose state is checkable against a public reef of hardware attestations, and registration requires a copper-signed hardware root tied to that machine. The bridge between workloads and identity is a challenge-response log a new identity can only join by completing real work on real silicon. Duplicating an identity therefore costs a distinct physical machine plus ongoing compute, roughly the price of a new server and its power draw per clone.
